We need the smallest positive integer satisfying  
\[
S\equiv 0 \pmod 9,\quad S\equiv 5 \pmod{10},\quad S\equiv 0 \pmod{11}.
\]
From \(S\equiv 0\pmod 9\) and \(S\equiv 0\pmod{11}\), we get \(S=99k\). Then
\[
99k\equiv 5 \pmod{10}.
\]
Since \(99\equiv -1\pmod{10}\),
\[
-k\equiv 5 \pmod{10}\quad\Rightarrow\quad k\equiv 5 \pmod{10}.
\]
The smallest positive \(k\) is \(5\), so
\[
S=99\cdot 5=495.
\]

\[
\boxed{495}
\]
